title: Parker's birthday party and the strings record
summary: At Parker's party Butler drank scotch among guests who forgot manners at the buffet, Parker threw him out in jest, and it was the last time he saw him; he later heard Parker with strings.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: And I went to the party and they was taking care corinne of business. They had/-- whatever that was --

Yeah, and so I stayed on the Black and White scotch and he kept watching me, all of them were happy. They had a big bowl, big bowl of those goodies, and (verbally demonstrating) -- forgetting all about their manners and everything. They was getting -- hog, pig pen effect. Yum. As the French call it, gruffing. That means they were -- all things goes to the

Yeah, and every man for himself. So, you know, he says, 'Man, what are you doing?' I was tearing that scotch up. My head was -- with the scotch, so he said, 'Well, look here, man, you go stumbling in -- get on out of here!' He screams, 'I thought you was my friend; You over there with that stuff, boy, get out of here!'
I said, 'Why, Mr. Parker, wait till I finish this first.' I don't know if he was high, I know I was high as I want to be and --
But he, I probably had a little more problems later when I woke up in the morning than he had but I was happy too, about it. It was the last time I saw my man.
But then, when I heard him with those strings, 'Autumn in New York,' I think it was 'Autumn in New York,' oh, that was the most beautiful thing I've heard.
And then, I reminisce about it, you know, when you are by yourself in a foreign country, you do a lot of thinking man. You don't have nothing to do but think, and that's the way it's happening, so --
